Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

robotcompR 0.1.0

  • Spatial mathematics: SO(2), SO(3), SE(2) and SE(3) objects, scalar-first unit quaternions, Euler angles for all 12 intrinsic sequences, Lie exponential and logarithm maps, adjoints and SO(3) Jacobians.
  • Rigid-body tree models with revolute, continuous, prismatic and fixed joints, standard and modified Denavit-Hartenberg models, and URDF import and export.
  • Forward kinematics, geometric and analytic Jacobians, manipulability.
  • Numerical inverse kinematics with Levenberg-Marquardt, damped least squares and pseudoinverse methods, joint limits and restarts.
  • Rigid-body dynamics: recursive Newton-Euler, composite rigid body and articulated body algorithms, gravity and Coriolis terms, energy, and ODE simulation.
  • Trajectories: cubic and quintic polynomials, trapezoidal profiles, timed waypoint paths and Cartesian straight lines.
  • Collision checking with convex primitives and GJK, environment and self-collision, and path checks.
  • Sampling-based planning with RRT, RRT-Connect, RRT* and PRM, plus shortcut smoothing.
  • Planar mobile robots: unicycle, differential drive, bicycle, odometry and pure pursuit.
  • Localization with extended and unscented Kalman filters and a particle filter.
  • Occupancy grid mapping, ray casting, inflation and A* search.
  • EKF-SLAM with known data association.
  • SE(2) and SE(3) pose graph optimization with Jacobians that stay valid for residual rotations near pi and a termination status.
  • The unscented Kalman filter works in a local tangent chart, so heading statistics stay consistent across the angle cut; every filter requires symmetric positive semidefinite covariances and validated measurements.
  • Particle filter prediction, EKF-SLAM updates and rigid-body dynamics use faster kernels (vectorized motion, a rank-two Joseph update and cached spatial inertias) with identical results.
  • EPA penetration depth for every convex pair, with certified bounds and a depth_known flag, and continuous path collision checking by conservative advancement.
  • Cartesian trajectories report spatial velocities and accelerations and can be converted to joint trajectories.
  • Nine vignettes and a pkgdown site.

Developed by Adam R Sophie.

Site built with pkgdown 2.2.1.
